FINDING #1 — CONFIRMED -> FIXED + GUARDED

Finding:
`project-context/BENCHMARK_EVALUATION_STRATEGY.md` still described the bounded automatic reviewer as the immediate implementation priority and the reviewer as the first active benchmark rung after PR #182 changed the authoritative release order to Core v1 first and deferred automatic reviewer/session-provider expansion.

Root cause:
The roadmap/current-state ownership documents were updated, but the active cross-capability benchmark strategy retained reviewer-first implementation wording that could reintroduce the superseded order during later major-release/architecture decisions.

Failure class:
A secondary active strategy document can retain an implementation-priority statement that conflicts with the authoritative roadmap even when roadmap-structure consistency tests remain green.

Fix:
- benchmark strategy now names CAP Core v1 freeze as the immediate implementation priority;
- automatic reviewer/session-provider expansion is explicitly deferred and not a Core-freeze prerequisite;
- reviewer benchmark integration/rung wording is classified as deferred specialist evaluation rather than current first implementation work.

Guard:
`tests/test_documentation_consistency.py::test_benchmark_strategy_does_not_restore_reviewer_first_release_priority` now requires the Core-first/deferred wording and rejects reintroduction of the exact reviewer-first priority/rung phrases.

pull_request.body:
## Summary

Fresh Stage Research after PR #159 physical qualification.

The target-Windows reviewer path on #159 proved automatic one-chat/one-Send/delivery/cleanup/structured capture, but the non-personalized Temporary profile then correctly returned ABSTAIN because disabling connected sources removed the exact full diff required by the review policy.

This PR records the architecture correction without starting another provider-adapter implementation:

- keep generic Delegation identity/state unchanged;
- retain `chatgpt-temporary` as an optional ephemeral clean-room profile and accepted physical evidence;
- separate conversation freshness from personalization/retention, read-source access and external mutation authority;
- select fresh ordinary ChatGPT as the next general-purpose provider direction;
- keep code review as one specialist consumer rather than the generic session architecture;
- defer implementation until after CAP Core v1 freeze, unless a concrete release-critical second consumer requires it earlier;
- keep manual fresh ordinary-ChatGPT review as current release assurance.

## Research

See `project-context/AGENT_SESSION_FRESH_CHAT_REENTRY.md`.

Decision:

`DEFER implementation now; select the ordinary-fresh direction for the next Agent Session provider stage.`

## External evidence

- OpenAI Temporary Chat now separates Personalized vs Unpersonalized modes.
- ChatGPT app permissions are a separate control surface from chat persistence/personalization.
- OpenAI documents GitHub-in-ChatGPT repository access as read-only for the standard GitHub app, while availability varies by product surface.
- Exact-source comparison against `openai/codex@41f9084b...` and `OpenHands/OpenHands@fd914595...` shows mature systems separate fresh session lifecycle from tool/permission policy.

## Scope

Documentation/research only. No production runtime, public tool surface, persistence format or authority code changes.
